ctx.x: He was an adventurer, a musical adven-

turer, wasn't he? I refer to Coleman Hawkins as a college of music, jazz music, any kind of music, jazz music in particular. Because that's the way -- but you can remember that I've met people like Art Tatum, and I put Coleman Hawkins in the same category. These people were what you call the ultimate in teachers of music. If anyone had any kind of ear at all, had any kind of knowledge, and was interested at all in learning, you had to learn something from these people. And as I said, this was my primary reason…

And as I said, Coleman Hawkins turned out to be a college of music for me, because he was involved in the highest form of progressions and music interpretation that there was around in those days. And he was considered to be one of the fathers of all times of this business (of) jazz music, you know. He had gone to Europe and on the strength of his ability he had created a reputation for himself that was incomparable. And he came back to the states in the midst of controversy about some of the young players like…
